translations.idiomatic: Tao Cheng

translations.literal: (son Lu)〉
translations.idiomatic: (son Lu)]〉

translations.literal: Chen Min Ding Xuan Wang Deren
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min, Ding Xuan, and Wang Deren

sentences.zh: （子一夔）〉

translations.literal: (son Yikui)〉
translations.idiomatic: (son Yikui)]〉

sentences.zh: 葉禎伍驥毛吉林錦郭緒姜昂

translations.literal: Ye Zhen Wu Ji Mao Ji Lin Jin Guo Xu Jiang Ang
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhen, Wu Ji, Mao Ji, Lin Jin, Guo Xu, and Jiang Ang

sentences.zh: （子龍）〉

translations.literal: (son Long)〉
translations.idiomatic: (son Long)]〉

sentences.zh: 陶成，字孔思，郁林人。

translations.literal: Tao Cheng, style name Kongsi, a man of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Cheng, whose style name was Kongsi, was a native of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，舉於鄉，除交阯鳳山典史。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign, he was recommended in the provincial examination and appointed clerk of Fengshan in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign he passed the provincial examination and was appointed clerk of Fengshan in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 尚書黃福知其賢，命署諒江府教授，交人化之。

translations.literal: Minister Huang Fu knew his worth and ordered him to act as instructor of Liangjiang Prefecture; the people of Jiaozhi were transformed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Huang Fu recognized his talent and had him serve as acting instructor of Liangjiang Prefecture, where he won over the people of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，遷山東按察司檢校，用薦擢大理評事。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was transferred to inspector of the Shandong surveillance commission, and on recommendation was promoted to reviewing censor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After his term ended he was moved to inspector of the Shandong surveillance commission, then promoted on recommendation to reviewing censor at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 正統中，以劉中敷薦，超擢浙江僉事。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign, on the recommendation of Liu Zhongfu he was promoted by exception to assistant commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign Liu Zhongfu recommended him, and he was promoted by exception to assistant commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 成有智略，遇事敢任。

translations.literal: Cheng had strategy and resourcefulness and dared to take responsibility when affairs arose.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was resourceful and bold in taking charge when crises arose.

sentences.zh: 倭犯桃渚，成密布釘板海沙中。

translations.literal: When the Wokou raided Taozhu, Cheng densely laid nail boards in the sea sand.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese pirates attacked Taozhu, Cheng had nail-studded boards hidden throughout the beach sand.

sentences.zh: 倭至，艤舟躍上，釘洞足背。

translations.literal: When the Wokou arrived, they moored their boats and leaped ashore; nails pierced the soles and backs of their feet.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates landed and leaped from their boats, the nails pierced their feet.

sentences.zh: 倭畏之，遠去。

translations.literal: The Wokou feared this and withdrew far away.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the pirates withdrew to distant waters.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進副使。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was advanced to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term he was promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 魯，字自強，蔭授新會丞。

translations.literal: Lu, style name Ziqiang, received the post of assistant magistrate of Xinhui by hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lu, whose style name was Ziqiang, inherited appointment as assistant magistrate of Xinhui.

sentences.zh: 當是時，廣西瑤流劫高、廉、惠、肇諸府，破城殺吏無虛月。

translations.literal: At that time Yao bands from Guangxi raided the prefectures of Gao, Lian, Hui, and Zhao, breaching cities and killing officials virtually every month.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yao raiders from Guangxi were pillaging the prefectures of Gao, Lian, Hui, and Zhao, storming cities and killing officials nearly every month.

sentences.zh: 香山、順德間，土寇蜂起，新會無賴子群聚應之。

translations.literal: Between Xiangshan and Shunde local bandits swarmed forth like bees, and ruffians of Xinhui gathered in groups to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Between Xiangshan and Shunde local bandits rose in swarms, and Xinhui's rowdies gathered to join them.

sentences.zh: 魯召父老語曰：「賊氣吞吾城，不早備且陷，若輩能率子弟捍禦乎？」

translations.literal: Lu summoned the elders and said: "The bandits' momentum will swallow our city; if we do not prepare early it will fall—can you lead your sons and younger kin to defend?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu summoned the village elders and said, "The rebels' momentum threatens to swallow our city. If we do not prepare now it will fall. Can you lead your sons and kin to defend it?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰「諾」。

translations.literal: All said "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "We will."

sentences.zh: 乃築堡寨，繕甲兵，練技勇，以孤城捍賊沖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built fortresses and stockades, repaired armor and weapons, trained the skilled and brave, and with a lone city held off the bandits' assault.
translations.idiomatic: He then built fortresses and stockades, repaired arms and armor, trained the militia, and held the isolated city against the rebels' onslaught.

sentences.zh: 建郭掘濠，布鐵蒺藜刺竹於外，城守大固。

translations.literal: He built outer walls and dug moats, laid iron caltrops and thorny bamboo outside, and the city's defense became greatly secure.
translations.idiomatic: He built outer walls, dug moats, and laid iron caltrops and thorny bamboo outside the walls until the city's defenses were formidable.

sentences.zh: 賊來犯，輒擊破之。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits came to attack, he always struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the rebels attacked, he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 天順七年，秩滿，巡撫葉盛上其績，就遷知縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianshun, when his term expired, Grand Coordinator Ye Sheng reported his achievements and he was promptly promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianshun, when his term ended, Grand Coordinator Ye Sheng reported his achievements and he was promoted on the spot to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 尋以破賊功，進廣州同知，仍知縣事。

translations.literal: Soon, for his merit in defeating bandits, he was advanced to vice prefect of Guangzhou while still administering the county.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for his success against the rebels, he was promoted to vice prefect of Guangzhou while continuing to administer the county.

sentences.zh: 成化二年從總督韓雍征大藤峽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he followed Grand Coordinator Han Yong to campaign against Dateng Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua he joined Grand Coordinator Han Yong's campaign against Dateng Gorge.

sentences.zh: 雍在軍嚴重，獨於魯未嘗不虛己。

translations.literal: Yong was stern and grave in the army, yet toward Lu alone he never failed to humble himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was famously stern in camp, yet with Lu alone he always deferred to his counsel.

sentences.zh: 用其策，輒有功。

translations.literal: Whenever he used Lu's stratagems, there was always merit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he adopted Lu's plans, victory followed.

sentences.zh: 雍請擢魯為僉事，專治新會、陽江、陽春、瀧水、新興諸縣兵。

translations.literal: Yong requested that Lu be promoted to assistant commissioner to specialize in commanding the troops of the counties Xinhui, Yangjiang, Yangchun, Longshui, and Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yong petitioned to promote Lu to assistant commissioner with sole charge of military affairs in Xinhui, Yangjiang, Yangchun, Longshui, and Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 其冬會參將王瑛破劇賊廖婆保等於欽、化二州，大獲，璽書嘉勞。

translations.literal: That winter, joining Vice Commander Wang Ying, he defeated the fierce bandit Liao Popao and others in the two prefectures Qin and Hua, gaining a great haul; an imperial edict commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, joining Vice Commander Wang Ying, he routed the notorious rebel Liao Popao and his followers in Qin and Hua prefectures in a major victory, for which the throne sent a sealed edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊首黃公漢等猖獗，偕參將夏鑒等連破之思恩、潯州。

translations.literal: The next year the bandit chiefs Huang Gonghan and others ran rampant; together with Vice Commander Xia Jian and others he repeatedly defeated them in Si'en and Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when rebel leaders including Huang Gonghan grew bold, he joined Vice Commander Xia Jian and others in a series of victories against them in Si'en and Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊陷石康，執知縣羅紳。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits seized Shikang and captured Magistrate Luo Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels overran Shikang and took Magistrate Luo Shen prisoner.

sentences.zh: 復偕鑒追擊至六菊山，敗之。

translations.literal: Again joining Jian he pursued in attack to Liuju Mountain and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Jian again in pursuit to Liuju Mountain and routed them.

sentences.zh: 兩廣自韓雍去，罷總督不設，帥臣觀望相推諉，寇盜滋蔓。

translations.literal: Since Han Yong left the Two Guangs, the grand coordinator post was abolished and not re-established; commanders looked on and shirked responsibility to one another, and bandits and robbers spread ever more.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Yong left the Two Guangs, the grand coordinator's office was left vacant; regional commanders looked on and passed blame to one another while banditry spread unchecked.

sentences.zh: 魯奏請重臣仍開府梧州，遂為永制。

translations.literal: Lu memorialized requesting that a senior official again open a headquarters at Wuzhou; this thereafter became a permanent institution.
translations.idiomatic: Lu memorialized that a senior official should again establish headquarters at Wuzhou, and this became permanent policy.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，課最，進副使。

translations.literal: When his term expired his performance rating was highest and he was advanced to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he received the top performance rating and was promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書余子俊奏其撫輯勞，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Minister of War Yu Zijun memorialized his toils in pacification and consolidation, and he was granted silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Yu Zijun reported his labors in pacifying the region, and the court rewarded him with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 魯治兵久。

translations.literal: Lu had long administered troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lu had commanded troops for many years.

sentences.zh: 賊剽兩粵，大者會剿，小者專征，所向奏捷。

translations.literal: When bandits raided the Two Yues, the large groups he joined in joint suppression, the small ones he campaigned against alone; wherever he went he reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels raided the Two Yues, he joined coordinated campaigns against the largest bands and led independent expeditions against smaller ones, winning wherever he marched.

sentences.zh: 賊讎之次骨，劫其郁林故居，焚誥命，發先塋，戕其族黨。

translations.literal: The bandits hated him to the marrow; they raided his old home in Yulin, burned his patent of appointment, opened his ancestors' tombs, and slaughtered his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hated him to the bone. They raided his family home in Yulin, burned his patent of appointment, desecrated his ancestors' graves, and slaughtered his kin.

sentences.zh: 魯聞大慟。

translations.literal: When Lu heard this he grieved greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was overcome with grief when he heard the news.

sentences.zh: 詔徙籍廣東，補給封誥，慰勞有加，益奮誌討賊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his household register moved to Guangdong, reissued his patent and edict of enfeoffment, added extra consolation and reward, and he redoubled his resolve to campaign against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered his household register transferred to Guangdong, reissued his patents of honor, and sent him special consolation, after which he fought the rebels with renewed zeal.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以征荔浦瑤功，增俸一級。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, for merit in campaigning against the Yao of Lipu, his salary was increased by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: In his twentieth year of service, for his campaign against the Yao of Lipu, his salary was raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 又九載，課最，進湖廣按察使，治兵兩廣如故。

translations.literal: After another nine years his performance rating was highest; he was advanced to surveillance commissioner of Huguang while still commanding troops in the Two Guangs as before.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years later, with another top performance rating, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Huguang while continuing to command troops in the Two Guangs as before.

sentences.zh: 郁林、陸川賊黃公定、胡公明等為亂，與參將歐磐分五路進討，大破之，毀賊巢一百三十。

translations.literal: The bandits Huang Gongding, Hu Gongming, and others of Yulin and Luchuan rose in rebellion; joining Vice Commander Ou Pan he advanced in five columns to campaign against them, inflicted a great defeat, and destroyed one hundred thirty bandit lairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels Huang Gongding, Hu Gongming, and others of Yulin and Luchuan rose up, he joined Vice Commander Ou Pan in a five-column advance, routed them, and destroyed one hundred thirty rebel strongholds.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，總督秦纮遣平德慶瑤，進湖廣右布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, Grand Coordinator Qin Hong dispatched him to pacify the Yao of Deqing; he was advanced to right administration commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, Grand Coordinator Qin Hong sent him to pacify the Yao of Deqing, after which he was promoted to right administration commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 魯言身居兩廣，而官以湖廣為名，於事體非便，乃改湖廣左布政使兼廣東按察副使，領嶺西道事。

translations.literal: Lu said that though his person resided in the Two Guangs, his office bore the name Huguang, which was inconvenient in substance; thereupon he was changed to left administration commissioner of Huguang concurrently vice surveillance commissioner of Guangdong, directing the affairs of the Lingxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Lu pointed out that although he served in the Two Guangs, his title bore the name Huguang, which was awkward in practice. He was therefore made left administration commissioner of Huguang while also serving as vice surveillance commissioner of Guangdong, with charge of the Lingxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 人稱之為「三廣公」。

translations.literal: People called him the "Lord of the Three Guangs."
translations.idiomatic: People called him the "Lord of the Three Guangs."

sentences.zh: 十一年，總督鄧廷瓚請官其子，俾統魯所募健卒備征討。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Grand Coordinator Deng Tingzan requested that his son be given an office post so that he might command the stalwart soldiers Lu had recruited, ready for campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Grand Coordinator Deng Tingzan petitioned to appoint Lu's son to command the elite troops Lu had raised for future campaigns.

sentences.zh: 乃授其子荊民錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon his son Jingmin was appointed a hundred-household guard of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingmin was accordingly appointed a hundred-household guard of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 是年，魯卒。

translations.literal: That year Lu died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lu died.

sentences.zh: 荊民復陳父功，遂進副千戶，世襲。

translations.literal: Jingmin again reported his father's achievements, and was thereupon advanced to vice thousand-household, hereditary in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmin then reported his father's further achievements and was promoted to vice thousand-household with a hereditary commission.

sentences.zh: 魯善撫士，多智計，謀定後戰。

translations.literal: Lu was skilled at winning over troops, had many stratagems, and fought only after plans were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu excelled at winning his men's loyalty, was full of stratagems, and never fought until his plans were set.

sentences.zh: 鑿池公署後，為亭其中，不置橋。

translations.literal: He dug a pool behind the government office and built a pavilion in its midst, placing no bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He dug a pool behind his yamen and built a pavilion in the middle of it, deliberately leaving no bridge.

sentences.zh: 夜則召部下計事。

translations.literal: At night he would summon subordinates to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At night he summoned his officers there one by one to discuss plans.

sentences.zh: 以版度一人，語畢，令退。

translations.literal: With a plank he ferried one person across; when the talk was finished he ordered him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He ferried each man across on a plank, and when the consultation ended sent him back alone.

sentences.zh: 如是凡數人，乃擇其長而參伍用之，故常得勝算而機不泄。

translations.literal: Thus for several persons in all, he then selected their strengths and combined and deployed them; therefore he constantly gained the upper hand while his designs were not leaked.
translations.idiomatic: After consulting several officers in this way, he combined their best ideas into his plans, which is why he so often won while keeping his intentions secret.

sentences.zh: 羽書狎至，戎裝宿戒，聲色不動。

translations.literal: Urgent dispatches arrived in close succession; he kept battle dress and overnight alerts, yet his voice and countenance did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Though urgent dispatches arrived in rapid succession, he slept in his armor on constant alert yet never showed alarm in voice or bearing.

sentences.zh: 審賊可乘，潛師出城，中夜合圍，曉輒奏凱。

translations.literal: When he judged the bandits vulnerable, he secretly led troops out of the city, encircled them at midnight, and by dawn always reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: When he judged the enemy vulnerable, he led troops out of the city in secret, surrounded them at midnight, and by dawn had already reported victory.

sentences.zh: 賊善偵，終不能得要領。

translations.literal: The bandits were skilled at reconnaissance yet ultimately could not grasp his essential moves.
translations.idiomatic: Though the rebels were skilled scouts, they never learned his true intentions.

sentences.zh: 歷官四十五年，始終不離兵事。

translations.literal: Through forty-five years in office he never left military affairs from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Over forty-five years in office he never left military affairs.

sentences.zh: 大小數十戰，凡斬馘二萬一千四百有奇，奪還被掠及撫安復業者十三萬七千有奇，兩廣人倚之如長城。

translations.literal: In several dozen battles large and small, he altogether beheaded and captured twenty-one thousand four hundred odd; those recovered from plunder and pacified to resume their livelihoods numbered one hundred thirty-seven thousand odd; the people of the Two Guangs relied on him as on the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: In several dozen engagements large and small he killed or captured more than twenty-one thousand four hundred enemies, recovered or resettled more than one hundred thirty-seven thousand people, and the people of the Two Guangs relied on him as they would on the Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 然魯將兵不專尚武，嘗言：「治寇賊，化之為先，不得已始殺之耳。」

translations.literal: Yet in commanding troops Lu did not exclusively esteem martial force; he once said: "In governing bandits and robbers, transforming them comes first; killing them is only when there is no alternative."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lu did not rely on force alone. He once said, "In dealing with bandits, transformation comes first; killing is only the last resort."

sentences.zh: 每平賊，率置縣建學以興教化。

translations.literal: Whenever he pacified bandits, he invariably established counties and built schools to promote civilizing instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he pacified a region he established counties and schools to promote civilizing education.

sentences.zh: 魯初為丞，年才弱冠，知縣王重勉之學。

translations.literal: When Lu first became assistant magistrate he was barely twenty; Magistrate Wang Chong urged him to study.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu first took office as assistant magistrate he was barely twenty, and Magistrate Wang Chong urged him to pursue his studies.

sentences.zh: 重故老儒，魯遂請執弟子禮。

translations.literal: Chong was an old Confucian scholar; Lu thereupon requested to perform the rites of a disciple toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was a venerable Confucian scholar, and Lu asked to become his formal disciple.

sentences.zh: 每晨，授經史講解而後視事。

translations.literal: Every morning he would receive instruction in the classics and histories with exposition, and only afterward attend to official business.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he received instruction in the classics and histories before turning to official business.

sentences.zh: 後重卒官，魯執喪如父禮，且資其二子。

translations.literal: Later Chong died in office; Lu observed mourning as for a father and moreover supported his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang later died in office, Lu mourned him as he would a father and supported his two sons.

sentences.zh: 又敬事名儒陳獻章，獻章亦重之。

translations.literal: He also respectfully served the renowned scholar Chen Xianzhang, and Xianzhang likewise esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: He also revered the renowned scholar Chen Xianzhang, who held him in equal regard.

sentences.zh: 宋陸秀夫、張世傑盡節崖山，未有廟祀，特為建祠，請祠額，賜名大忠。

translations.literal: The Song loyalists Lu Xiufu and Zhang Shijie died loyal at Yashan yet had no temple sacrifice; he specially built a shrine for them, requested a shrine plaque, and was granted the name Dazhong, Great Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Song loyalists Lu Xiufu and Zhang Shijie, who died defending Yashan, had no temple in the region. Lu built a shrine for them, petitioned for an official plaque, and received the name Dazhong, Great Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，魯歿三十載矣，新會人思其德，頌於朝，賜祠祀之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, thirty years after Lu's death, the people of Xinhui mindful of his virtue praised him at court, and a shrine sacrifice was granted in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, thirty years after Lu's death, the people of Xinhui, remembering his virtue, petitioned the court in his praise, and he was granted official shrine worship.

sentences.zh: 陳敏，陜西華亭人。

translations.literal: Chen Min, a man of Huating in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min was a native of Huating in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 宣德時，為四川茂州知州。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign he served as magistrate of Maozhou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign he served as magistrate of Maozhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 遭喪去官，所部諸長官司及番民百八十人詣闕奏言：「州僻處邊僥萬山中，與松藩、疊溪諸番鄰，歲被其患。

translations.literal: When he suffered bereavement and left office, the chieftain offices under his jurisdiction and one hundred eighty native subjects went to the capital and memorialized: "The prefecture lies remote in the border wilds among myriad mountains, neighboring the Fan of Songpan, Diexi, and elsewhere, and every year suffers their harm.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office to observe mourning, the native chieftains under his jurisdiction and one hundred eighty tribal subjects traveled to the capital and petitioned: "Our prefecture lies remote in the border mountains, neighboring the tribes of Songpan, Diexi, and elsewhere, and suffers their raids year after year.

sentences.zh: 自敏蒞州，撫馭有方，民得安業。

translations.literal: Since Min took office in the prefecture, his pacification and control have been well ordered, and the people have obtained secure livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Since Minister Min took office, his governance has been exemplary and the people live in peace.

sentences.zh: 今以憂去職，軍民失所依。

translations.literal: Now because of mourning he has left office, and soldiers and civilians have lost what they relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has left on account of mourning, soldiers and civilians have lost their protector.

sentences.zh: 乞矜念遠方，還此良牧。」

translations.literal: We beg compassionate regard for a distant region and the return of this excellent shepherd."
translations.idiomatic: We beg the court to show compassion for this distant region and restore this worthy magistrate."

sentences.zh: 帝立報可。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately approved in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately approved the request.

sentences.zh: 正統中，九載滿，軍民復請留。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign, when nine years were complete, soldiers and civilians again requested that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign, when his nine-year term ended, soldiers and civilians again petitioned for his retention.

sentences.zh: 進成都府同知，視茂州事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice prefect of Chengdu Prefecture while overseeing Maozhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice prefect of Chengdu while continuing to administer Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 都司徐甫言，敏及指揮孫敬在職公勤，群番信服。

translations.literal: The regional military commission's Xu Fu reported that Min and Commander Sun Jing were diligent and upright in office, and all the Fan trusted and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu of the regional military commission reported that Min and Commander Sun Jing were diligent and upright in office, and that all the tribes trusted them.

sentences.zh: 章下都御史王翺等核實，進敏右參議，仍視州事。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to Censor-in-Chief Wang Ao and others to verify; Min was advanced to right assistant administration commissioner while still overseeing prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to Censor-in-Chief Wang Ao and others for verification, after which Min was promoted to right assistant administration commissioner while still administering the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以監司秩蒞州，前此未有也。

translations.literal: To hold a prefecture at surveillance-commissioner rank—there had never been such a thing before.
translations.idiomatic: Never before had a surveillance commissioner ranked official been appointed to govern a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 黑虎寨番掠近境，為官軍所獲。

translations.literal: Fan of Heihu Stockade raided the near borderlands and were captured by government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tribesmen from Heihu Stockade raided the borderlands and were captured by government troops.

sentences.zh: 敏從其俗，與誓而遣之。

translations.literal: Min followed their custom, swore an oath with them, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Min followed local custom, exchanged oaths with them, and released them.

sentences.zh: 既復出掠，為巡按御史陳員韜所劾。

translations.literal: After they again came out to raid, they were impeached by touring censor Chen Yuntao.
translations.idiomatic: When they raided again, Touring Censor Chen Yuntao impeached him.

sentences.zh: 詔貰之。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne pardoned him by edict.

sentences.zh: 提督都御史寇深器其才，言敏往來撫恤番人，贊理軍政，乞別除知州，俾敏專戎務。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor-in-Chief Kou Shen valued his talent and said Min went back and forth to comfort and succor the Fan, assisting in military administration, and begged that a separate appointment be made as magistrate so that Min might specialize in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor-in-Chief Kou Shen valued his talent and reported that Min traveled constantly to comfort the tribes and assist in military administration. He petitioned to appoint a separate magistrate so that Min could devote himself entirely to military affairs.

sentences.zh: 吏部以敏蒞茂久，別除恐未悉番情，猝難馴服，宜增設同知一人佐之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel said Min had long held Maozhou and a separate appointment might not fully understand Fan conditions, making sudden control difficult; one vice prefect should be added to assist.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel replied that Min had governed Maozhou for so long that a new appointee might not understand tribal affairs and could not quickly win their trust. It recommended adding a vice prefect to assist him instead.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 敏既以參議治州，其體儷監司。

translations.literal: Min now governed the prefecture as assistant commissioner, his standing equal to a surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Min now governed the prefecture at assistant commissioner rank, with standing equal to a surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遂劾按察使陳泰無故杖死番人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he impeached Surveillance Commissioner Chen Tai for beating a Fan person to death without cause.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Surveillance Commissioner Chen Tai for beating a tribesman to death without cause.

sentences.zh: 泰亦訐敏，帝不問。

translations.literal: Tai also denounced Min; the Emperor made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Tai counter-impeached Min, but the Emperor took no action against either.

sentences.zh: 而泰下獄論罪。

translations.literal: Yet Tai was imprisoned and sentenced for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Tai, however, was imprisoned and convicted.

sentences.zh: 景泰改元，參議滿九載，進右參政，視州事如前。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title to Jingtai, when nine years as assistant commissioner were complete, he was advanced to right administration commissioner, overseeing prefectural affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign, when his nine-year term as assistant commissioner ended, he was promoted to right administration commissioner while continuing to administer the prefecture as before.

sentences.zh: 蒞州二十余年，威信大行，番民胥悅。

translations.literal: He held the prefecture for more than twenty years; his prestige and authority greatly flourished, and all the Fan subjects were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the prefecture for more than twenty years, his authority became formidable, and all the tribal peoples were content.

sentences.zh: 秩漸高，諸監司郡守反位其下，同事多忌之者。

translations.literal: As his rank gradually rose, the various surveillance commissioners and prefectural magistrates were inversely placed beneath him; many colleagues envied him.
translations.idiomatic: As his rank rose, surveillance commissioners and prefectural magistrates found themselves subordinate to him, and many colleagues grew jealous.

sentences.zh: 為按察使張淑所劾，罷去。

translations.literal: He was impeached by Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Shu and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Shu impeached him, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 丁瑄，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Ding Xuan—his native place is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xuan was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 正統間為御史。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign he served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 初，福建多礦盜，命御史柳華捕之。

translations.literal: Initially Fujian had many mining bandits; the court ordered Censor Liu Hua to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: At first Fujian was plagued by mining bandits, and the court appointed Censor Liu Hua to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 華令村聚皆置望樓，編民為甲，擇其豪為長，得自置兵仗，督民巡僥。

translations.literal: Hua ordered every village settlement to set up watch towers, organized the people into militia companies, chose the powerful among them as leaders, allowed them to provide their own weapons, and supervised the people in patrolling the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Hua ordered every village to build watch towers, organized the populace into militia companies under local strongmen, allowed them to arm themselves, and supervised border patrols.

sentences.zh: 沙縣佃人鄧茂七素無賴，既為甲長，益以氣役屬鄉民。

translations.literal: Deng Maoqi of Shaxian, a tenant farmer who had always been a ruffian, once made company leader used his forceful manner all the more to dominate the village folk.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Maoqi, a tenant farmer of Shaxian who had long been a ruffian, became a militia captain and used his authority to bully the villagers.

sentences.zh: 其俗佃人輸租外，例饋田主。

translations.literal: By local custom, beyond paying rent tenants also routinely presented gifts to the landowner.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom required tenants to present gifts to their landlords in addition to paying rent.

sentences.zh: 茂七倡其黨令毋饋，而田主自往受粟。

translations.literal: Maoqi urged his faction to stop presenting gifts and instead have the landowner come in person to receive the grain.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqi urged his followers to stop sending gifts and instead require landlords to come collect the grain themselves.

sentences.zh: 田主訴於縣，縣逮茂七，不赴。

translations.literal: The landowner complained to the county; the county arrested Maoqi, but he did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: A landlord complained to the county magistrate, who summoned Maoqi, but he refused to appear.

sentences.zh: 下巡檢追攝，茂七殺弓兵數人。

translations.literal: The subordinate patrol inspector was sent to pursue and seize him; Maoqi killed several bow soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When a patrol inspector was sent to arrest him, Maoqi killed several government archers.

sentences.zh: 上官聞，遣軍三百捕之。

translations.literal: Superiors heard of this and dispatched three hundred troops to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: When superiors learned of this, they sent three hundred troops to capture him.

sentences.zh: 被殺傷幾盡，巡檢及知縣並遇害。

translations.literal: They were nearly all killed or wounded; the patrol inspector and the magistrate were both slain.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly all were killed or wounded, including the patrol inspector and the county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 茂七遂大剽略，偽稱「鏟平王」，設官屬，黨數萬人，陷二十余縣。

translations.literal: Maoqi thereupon launched great pillaging, falsely styled himself "King Who Levels All," established official posts, gathered a faction of tens of thousands, and seized more than twenty counties.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqi then launched large-scale raids, proclaimed himself the "King Who Levels All," established a rebel government, rallied tens of thousands of followers, and overran more than twenty counties.

sentences.zh: 都指揮範真、指揮彭璽等先後被殺。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Fan Zhen, Commander Peng Xi, and others were killed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Fan Zhen, Commander Peng Xi, and others were killed in succession.

sentences.zh: 時福建參政交阯人宋新，賄王振得遷左布政使，侵漁貪惡，民不能堪，益相率從亂。

translations.literal: At that time the Fujian administration commissioner Song Xin, a man of Jiaozhi, bribed Wang Zhen to obtain transfer as left administration commissioner; he plundered and was greedy and vicious—the people could not endure it and increasingly joined the rebellion in groups.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fujian's administration commissioner Song Xin, a native of Jiaozhi, bribed the powerful eunuch Wang Zhen for promotion to left administration commissioner. His extortion and cruelty drove the people to join the rebellion in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 東南騷動。

translations.literal: The southeast was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，茂七圍延平。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, Maoqi besieged Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, Maoqi besieged Yanping.

sentences.zh: 刷卷御史張海登城撫諭。

translations.literal: Document-reviewing censor Zhang Hai ascended the city wall to comfort and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Document-reviewing Censor Zhang Hai mounted the city wall to address the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊訴乞貰死，免三年徭役，即解散為良民。

translations.literal: The bandits pleaded begging pardon for their lives, exemption from three years of corvée labor, and that they would then disband and become good subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pleaded for their lives, exemption from three years of corvée labor, and promised to disband and return to peaceful life.

sentences.zh: 海以聞。

translations.literal: Hai reported this upward.
translations.idiomatic: Hai reported this to the court.

sentences.zh: 命瑄往招討，以都督劉聚、僉都御史張楷大軍繼其後。

translations.literal: The court ordered Xuan to go to summon and suppress them, with Regional Commander Liu Ju and Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kai's great army following after.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Xuan to negotiate and suppress the rebels, with Regional Commander Liu Ju and Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kai's main force to follow.

sentences.zh: 瑄既至，先令人賫敕往撫。

translations.literal: Once Xuan arrived, he first sent someone bearing an imperial edict to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival, Xuan first sent an envoy bearing an imperial edict offering amnesty.

sentences.zh: 茂七不肯降，瑄馳赴沙縣圖之。

translations.literal: Maoqi refused to surrender; Xuan galloped to Shaxian to plan against him.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqi refused to surrender, and Xuan rushed to Shaxian to plan his capture.

sentences.zh: 賊首林宗政等萬余人攻後坪，欲立寨。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Lin Zongzheng and more than ten thousand others attacked Houping, intending to establish a stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leader Lin Zongzheng and more than ten thousand followers attacked Houping, intending to establish a stronghold.

sentences.zh: 瑄令通判倪冕等率眾先據要害，而身與都指揮雍埜等邀其歸路，斬賊二百余級，獲其渠陳阿巖。

translations.literal: Xuan ordered Vice Prefect Ni Mian and others to lead the masses first to seize strategic points, while he himself with Regional Commander Yong Ye and others intercepted their route of return, beheading more than two hundred bandits and capturing their ringleader Chen Ayan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan ordered Vice Prefect Ni Mian and others to seize strategic positions while he personally joined Regional Commander Yong Ye in cutting off the rebels' retreat, killing more than two hundred and capturing their leader Chen Ayan.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，瑄誘賊復攻延平，督眾軍分道沖擊。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year, Xuan lured the bandits to attack Yanping again and supervised the armies in charging attacks along separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The following February, Xuan lured the rebels into attacking Yanping again, then directed his forces in a multi-pronged assault.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗，遁走，指揮劉福追之，遂斬茂七，招脅從復業。

translations.literal: The bandits suffered a great defeat and fled; Commander Liu Fu pursued them, thereupon beheaded Maoqi, and summoned the coerced followers to resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed and fled. Commander Liu Fu pursued them, killed Maoqi, and persuaded the coerced followers to return to peaceful life.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復擒其黨林子得等。

translations.literal: Before long he again captured his faction members Lin Zide and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he captured Maoqi's followers Lin Zide and others.

sentences.zh: 尤溪賊首鄭永祖率四千人攻延平。

translations.literal: The Youxi bandit chief Zheng Yongzu led four thousand men to attack Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: The Youxi rebel leader Zheng Yongzu led four thousand men in an attack on Yanping.

sentences.zh: 瑄偕埜等邀擊，擒之，斬首五百有奇，余黨潰散。

translations.literal: Xuan together with Ye and others intercepted and struck; they captured him, beheaded more than five hundred odd, and the remaining faction scattered in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan joined Ye and others in an ambush, captured Zheng, killed more than five hundred rebels, and the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 楷之監大軍討賊也，至建寧頓不進，日置酒賦詩為樂。

translations.literal: When Kai was supervising the great army to campaign against bandits, he reached Jianning and halted without advancing, daily setting out wine and composing poetry for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: When Kai was appointed to supervise the main army against the rebels, he halted at Jianning without advancing, spending his days feasting and composing poetry.

sentences.zh: 聞瑄破賊，則馳至延平攘其功。

translations.literal: When he heard Xuan had defeated the bandits, he galloped to Yanping to seize his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Xuan had defeated the rebels, he rushed to Yanping to claim the credit.

sentences.zh: 瑄被脅依違具奏。

translations.literal: Xuan was coerced and in his memorial was evasive and contradictory.
translations.idiomatic: Under pressure, Xuan filed an equivocal report.

sentences.zh: 福不能平，訴之。

translations.literal: Fu could not accept this and appealed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fu, unable to accept this injustice, appealed to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔責瑄具狀。

translations.literal: An edict reproached Xuan and ordered a full report of the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked Xuan and ordered a full factual report.

sentences.zh: 楷等皆獲罪。

translations.literal: Kai and others were all punished for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Kai and his associates were all punished.

sentences.zh: 瑄有功不問，功亦竟不錄。

translations.literal: Xuan was not questioned despite his merit, yet his merit was ultimately not recorded either.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was not punished, but his achievements were never officially recorded.

sentences.zh: 茂七雖死，其從子伯孫等復熾。

translations.literal: Though Maoqi was dead, his followers Bo and Sun and others again flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Though Maoqi was dead, his nephews Bo and Sun and other followers revived the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷更遣陳懋等以大軍討，瑄乃還朝。

translations.literal: The court again dispatched Chen Mao and others with a great army to campaign; Xuan then returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Chen Mao and others with a main army to continue the campaign, and Xuan returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，出為廣東副使，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai he went out as vice commissioner of Guangdong and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign he was appointed vice commissioner of Guangdong, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 當是時，浙、閩盜所在剽掠為民患。

translations.literal: At that time bandits in Zhe and Min everywhere raided and plundered, becoming a calamity for the people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits in Zhejiang and Fujian were raiding everywhere and plaguing the populace.

sentences.zh: 將帥率玩寇，而文吏勵民兵拒賊，往往多斬獲。

translations.literal: Generals for the most part treated bandits lightly, while civil officials roused militia to resist bandits and often achieved many beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Military commanders for the most part neglected the threat, while civil officials rallied militia to resist the rebels and often won significant victories.

sentences.zh: 閩則有張瑛、王得仁之屬。

translations.literal: In Min there were Zhang Ying, Wang Deren, and their kind.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian there were men such as Zhang Ying and Wang Deren.

sentences.zh: 浙江則金華知府石瑁擒遂昌賊蘇才於蘭溪。

translations.literal: In Zhejiang, Jinhua Prefect Shi Yao captured the Suicang bandit Su Cai at Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhejiang, Jinhua Prefect Shi Yao captured the Suicang rebel Su Cai at Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 處州知府張佑擊敗賊眾，擒斬千余人。

translations.literal: Chuzhou Prefect Zhang You defeated the bandit masses, capturing and beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou Prefect Zhang You defeated a rebel force, capturing and killing more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 於是帝降敕，數詰讓諸將帥。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor issued an edict repeatedly reproaching the various generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then issued repeated edicts rebuking the military commanders.

sentences.zh: 都指揮鄧安等因歸咎於前御史柳華。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Deng An and others thereupon shifted blame onto the former censor Liu Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Deng An and others shifted the blame onto the former censor Liu Hua.

sentences.zh: 時王振方欲殺朝士威眾，命逮華。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhen wished to kill court officials to awe the masses and ordered Hua arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, seeking to intimidate the court by executing officials, ordered Hua's arrest.

sentences.zh: 華已出為山東副使，聞命，仰藥死。

translations.literal: Hua had already gone out as vice commissioner of Shandong; on hearing the order he took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hua had already been transferred to vice commissioner of Shandong. On hearing the order he took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 詔籍其家，男戍邊，婦女沒入浣衣局。

translations.literal: An edict registered his household property for confiscation; males were banished to the frontier, women entered the laundry bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The court confiscated his property, banished his sons to the frontier, and sent the women of his household to the imperial laundry.

sentences.zh: 而御史汪澄、柴文顯亦以是得罪。

translations.literal: Censors Wang Cheng and Chai Wenxian also offended on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Wang Cheng and Chai Wenxian were also punished on related charges.

sentences.zh: 初，澄按福建，以茂七亂，檄浙江、江西會討。

translations.literal: Initially, when Cheng inspected Fujian, because of Maoqi's rebellion he issued orders to Zhejiang and Jiangxi to join in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng was touring Fujian, he issued orders to Zhejiang and Jiangxi to join the campaign against Maoqi's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 尋以賊方議降，止兵毋進。

translations.literal: Soon because the bandits were negotiating surrender, he halted the troops and forbade advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels began negotiating surrender, he ordered the armies to halt.

sentences.zh: 既知賊無降意，復趣進兵，而賊已不可制。

translations.literal: Once he knew the bandits had no intent to surrender, he again urged advance—but the bandits could no longer be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the rebels had no intention of surrendering, he ordered the advance resumed, but by then the rebellion was beyond control.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡按御史黃英恐得罪，具白澄止兵狀，兵部因劾澄失機。

translations.literal: Zhejiang touring censor Huang Ying, fearing punishment, fully reported Cheng's halting of troops; the Ministry of War thereupon impeached Cheng for missing the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Touring Censor Huang Ying, fearing blame, reported Cheng's order to halt the troops, and the Ministry of War impeached Cheng for missing the opportunity.

sentences.zh: 福建三司亦言，賊初起，按臣柴文顯匿不奏，釀成今患。

translations.literal: The three offices of Fujian also said that when the bandits first arose, touring official Chai Wenxian concealed it and did not memorialize, brewing the present calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian's three provincial offices also reported that when the rebellion first broke out, touring official Chai Wenxian had concealed it from the court, allowing the present disaster.

sentences.zh: 遂俱下吏。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were handed to the judicial clerks.
translations.idiomatic: All were accordingly imprisoned and tried.

sentences.zh: 獄成，詔磔文顯，籍其家。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, an edict ordered Wenxian dismembered and his household registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: When the trials concluded, Wenxian was sentenced to dismemberment and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 澄棄市。

translations.literal: Cheng was executed by dismemberment in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 而宋新及按察使方冊等十人俱坐斬。

translations.literal: Song Xin and Surveillance Commissioner Fang Ce and ten others all sat for execution by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xin, Surveillance Commissioner Fang Ce, and ten others were all sentenced to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，謫驛丞。

translations.literal: They encountered an amnesty and were demoted to post-station assistants.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty commuted their sentences to demotion to post-station assistants.

sentences.zh: 天順初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun their offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign their offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 論者謂華所建置未為過，澄、文顯罪不至死。

translations.literal: Commentators said what Hua had established was not excessive, and Cheng and Wenxian's crimes did not merit death.
translations.idiomatic: Later commentators held that Hua's policies had not been excessive and that Cheng and Wenxian did not deserve death.

sentences.zh: 武將不能滅賊，反罪文吏。

translations.literal: Military officers could not exterminate the bandits yet instead punished civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: The military had failed to suppress the rebels yet civil officials were punished instead.

sentences.zh: 華、文顯至與叛逆同科，失刑實由王振雲。

translations.literal: Hua and Wenxian were even classed with rebellion—the perversion of justice truly stemmed from Wang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: That Hua and Wenxian were punished as rebels was a perversion of justice attributable to Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 華，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Hua was a man of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was a native of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 文顯，浙江建德人。

translations.literal: Wenxian was a man of Jiande in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxian was a native of Jiande in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 澄仁和人。

translations.literal: Cheng was a man of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was a native of Renhe.

sentences.zh: 王得仁，名仁，以字行，新建人。

translations.literal: Wang Deren—his given name was Ren, but he went by his style name—was a man of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Deren, whose given name was Ren but who was known by his style name, was a native of Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 本謝姓，父避仇外家，因冒王氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Xie; his father fled a feud to his wife's family and therefore assumed the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: His family surname was originally Xie. His father, fleeing a blood feud, took refuge with his wife's family and adopted the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 得仁五歲喪母，哀號如成人。

translations.literal: Deren lost his mother at five; he wailed as if an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Deren lost his mother at the age of five and mourned with the grief of an adult.

sentences.zh: 初為衛吏，以才薦授汀州府經歷。

translations.literal: He first served as a guard clerk; on recommendation for talent he was appointed intendant of Tingzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a guard clerk and was recommended for his ability to the post of intendant of Tingzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 廉能勤敏，上下愛之。

translations.literal: Upright, capable, diligent, and keen, he was loved above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Honest, capable, diligent, and alert, he was beloved by superiors and subordinates alike.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當遷，軍民數千人乞留，詔增秩再任。

translations.literal: When his term expired and he was due for transfer, several thousand soldiers and civilians begged that he be retained; an edict increased his rank and reappointed him.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he was due for transfer, several thousand soldiers and civilians petitioned for his retention, and the court increased his rank and reappointed him.

sentences.zh: 居三年，推官缺，英宗從軍民請，就令遷擢。

translations.literal: After three years in office the post of investigating censor was vacant; Emperor Yingzong acceded to the soldiers' and civilians' request and had him promoted on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, when the post of investigating censor fell vacant, Emperor Yingzong granted the people's petition and promoted him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 數辯冤獄，卻饋遺，抑鎮守內臣苛索，政績益著。

translations.literal: He repeatedly redressed wrongful cases, refused gifts, and curbed the exactions of the garrison eunuchs; his administrative achievements grew ever more notable.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly overturned wrongful convictions, refused bribes, and curbed the exactions of garrison eunuchs, and his reputation for effective governance grew.

sentences.zh: 沙縣賊陳政景，故鄧茂七黨也。

translations.literal: The Shaxian bandit Chen Zhengjing was a former follower of Deng Maoqi.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaxian rebel Chen Zhengjing was a former follower of Deng Maoqi.

sentences.zh: 糾清流賊藍得隆等攻城。

translations.literal: He gathered the Qingliu bandit Lan Delong and others to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: He joined forces with the Qingliu rebel Lan Delong and others to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 得仁與守將及知府劉能擊敗之，擒政景等八十四人，余賊驚潰。

translations.literal: Deren together with the garrison commander and Prefect Liu Neng defeated them, capturing Zhengjing and eighty-four others; the remaining bandits fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Deren joined the garrison commander and Prefect Liu Neng in defeating them, capturing Zhengjing and eighty-four others while the rest fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 諸將議窮搜，得仁恐濫及百姓，下令招撫，辨釋難民三百人。

translations.literal: The generals discussed exhaustive search; Deren feared indiscriminate harm to common people and ordered pacification by summons, distinguishing and releasing three hundred refugees.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals proposed a thorough manhunt, Deren feared innocent civilians would be harmed and ordered a policy of amnesty, releasing three hundred refugees who had been wrongly detained.

sentences.zh: 都指揮馬雄得通賊者姓名，將按籍行戮，得仁力請焚其籍。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Ma Xiong obtained the names of those who had communicated with bandits and was about to execute them according to the register; Deren strongly begged that the register be burned.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Ma Xiong obtained a list of those who had aided the rebels and prepared to execute them by the register. Deren strongly petitioned to have the list burned.

sentences.zh: 賊復寇寧化，率兵往援，斬首甚眾。

translations.literal: The bandits again raided Ninghua; he led troops to relieve it and beheaded a great many.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels again attacked Ninghua, he led troops to the relief and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 民多自拔歸，賊勢益衰。

translations.literal: Many of the people came out of their own accord to submit; the bandits' momentum daily waned.
translations.idiomatic: Many civilians voluntarily returned to government control, and rebel strength steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 賊退屯將樂，得仁將追滅之，俄遘疾。

translations.literal: The bandits withdrew and encamped at Jiangle; Deren was about to pursue and destroy them when he suddenly fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew to Jiangle, and Deren was preparing to pursue and destroy them when he suddenly fell ill.

sentences.zh: 眾欲輿歸就醫，得仁不可，曰：「吾一動，賊必長驅。」

translations.literal: The masses wished to carry him back in a litter for medical treatment; Deren would not allow it and said: "If I move once, the bandits will surely drive deep in pursuit."
translations.idiomatic: His officers wished to carry him back for treatment, but Deren refused, saying, "If I withdraw, the rebels will advance unchecked."

sentences.zh: 乃起坐帳中，諭將吏戮力平賊，遂卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sat up in his tent and instructed the generals and officials to exert all strength to pacify the bandits, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He then sat up in his tent and urged his officers to exert every effort to pacify the rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 時正統十四年夏也。

translations.literal: This was the summer of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: This was the summer of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 軍民哀慟。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians grieved in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 喪還，哭奠者道路相屬，多繪像祀之。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, mourners offering sacrifice lined the roads in succession; many painted his portrait for worship.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin was borne home, mourners lined the roads, and many painted his portrait for veneration.

sentences.zh: 天順末，吏民乞建祠。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianshun, officials and people begged to build a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianshun reign, officials and commoners petitioned for a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 有司為請，詔如廣東楊信民故事，春秋致祭。

translations.literal: The responsible offices petitioned on their behalf; an edict followed the precedent of Guangdong's Yang Xinmin, with sacrifices in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities petitioned on their behalf, and the court granted seasonal sacrifices in spring and autumn, following the precedent of Yang Xinmin of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 子一夔，天順四年舉進士第一。

translations.literal: His son Yikui in the fourth year of Tianshun placed first in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yikui placed first in the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 授修撰，進左諭德。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler, then advanced to left preceptor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin compiler and later promoted to left preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 成化七年，彗星見。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chenghua a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chenghua a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 應詔陳五事：請正宮闈，親大臣，開言路，慎刑獄，戒妄費。

translations.literal: In response to an edict he presented five matters: request to rectify the inner palace, draw near to great ministers, open the path of speech, be cautious in criminal punishment, and guard against reckless expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: In response to an imperial edict he presented five recommendations: rectify the inner palace, draw close to senior ministers, open channels for remonstrance, exercise caution in criminal justice, and guard against wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 語極剴摯，被旨切責。

translations.literal: His words were extremely earnest and sincere; he received an imperial rescript of stern reproach.
translations.idiomatic: His language was forthright and impassioned, and he received a stern imperial rebuke.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 正德中，謚文莊。

translations.literal: During Zhengde he was given the posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he was granted the posthumous title Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 葉禎，字夢吉，高要人。

translations.literal: Ye Zhen, style Mengji, was a native of Gaoyao.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhen, styled Mengji, was from Gaoyao.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，授潯州府同知。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination and was appointed vice prefect of Xunzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the provincial examination, he was appointed vice prefect of Xunzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 補鳳翔，調慶遠。

translations.literal: He was posted to Fengxiang, then transferred to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Fengxiang and was later transferred to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 兩廣瑤賊蜂起，列郡鹹被害，將吏率縮朒觀望。

translations.literal: Yao bandits in the Two Guangs swarmed up like bees; the various prefectures all alike suffered harm, and commanders and officials for the most part shrank back and watched from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Yao rebels rose in swarms across the Two Guangs, and prefecture after prefecture fell victim; most commanders and officials cowered and held back.

sentences.zh: 禎誓不與賊俱生，募健兒日訓練。

translations.literal: Zhen swore not to live together with the bandits, recruited stalwart youths, and trained them daily.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen vowed that he and the rebels could not both live, recruited stalwart fighters, and drilled them every day.

sentences.zh: 峒酋韋父強數敗官軍，禎生縶之，其黨忿，悉眾攻城。

translations.literal: The cave chieftain Wei Fuqiang had repeatedly defeated government troops; Zhen captured him alive, and his faction, enraged, mustered all their forces to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: The cave chieftain Wei Fuqiang had repeatedly routed government forces. Zhen took him alive, and his followers, furious, rallied their full strength to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 旗山守將擁兵不救。

translations.literal: The defending general at Qishan held his troops and did not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander at Qishan kept his troops idle and refused to come to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 禎率健兒出戰，賊卻去。

translations.literal: Zhen led his stalwart youths out to battle, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen led his fighters out to meet them, and the rebels fell back.

sentences.zh: 旋躡禎，戰相當，禎子公榮殲焉。

translations.literal: Presently they pursued close on Zhen's heels; the fighting was evenly matched, and Zhen's son Gongrong was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: They soon pressed hard on Zhen's heels. In the fierce exchange, his son Gongrong was killed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，賊圍雞刺諸村，禎率三百人趨赴。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits besieged the villages around Jici; Zhen led three hundred men in haste to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels besieged the villages around Jici, and Zhen rushed to their relief with three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 道遇賊人頭山下，鏖戰，禎被數槍，手刃賊一人，與從子官慶及三百人皆死。

translations.literal: On the road he encountered the bandits below Rentou Mountain; they fought fiercely. Zhen was struck by several spears, personally slew one bandit with his blade, and he, his nephew Guanqing, and all three hundred men died.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he met the rebels below Rentou Mountain and fought a desperate battle. Zhen took several spear wounds, cut down one rebel with his own hand, and fell together with his nephew Guanqing and all three hundred of his men.

sentences.zh: 時天順三年正月晦也。

translations.literal: It was then the last day of the first month of the third year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: This was the last day of the first lunar month in the third year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 嶺南素無雪，是夜大雷電，雪深尺許。

translations.literal: South of the ranges had never known snow; that night came great thunder and lightning, and the snow lay more than a foot deep.
translations.idiomatic: Snow was unknown in Lingnan, yet that night thunder cracked and lightning flashed, and snow piled more than a foot deep.

sentences.zh: 賊釋圍去，諸村獲全。

translations.literal: The bandits lifted the siege and departed; the villages were all preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke off the siege and withdrew, and the villages were spared.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈朝列大夫、廣西參議，守臣為立廟祀之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted Court Rank Grand Master and Guangxi Assistant Administration Commissioner; the defending officials built a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted the rank of Court Rank Grand Master and Guangxi Assistant Administration Commissioner, and local officials erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 伍驥，字德良，安福人。

translations.literal: Wu Ji, style Deliang, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ji, styled Deliang, was from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the fifth year of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 莊重寡言笑，見義敢為。

translations.literal: Solemn and dignified, he spoke and laughed little; when he saw righteousness he dared act.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and reserved, he spoke little and laughed less, yet he acted boldly whenever justice demanded it.

sentences.zh: 天順七年巡按福建。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianshun he toured and inspected Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianshun he served as touring censor of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 先是，上杭賊起，都指揮僉事丁泉，汶上人，善捍禦。

translations.literal: Earlier, bandits had risen at Shanghang; the assistant regional commander Ding Quan, a native of Wen, was skilled at defense.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, rebels had risen at Shanghang. The assistant regional commander Ding Quan, a native of Wen County, was an able defender.

sentences.zh: 賊屢攻城，皆為所卻。

translations.literal: The bandits repeatedly attacked the city, and each time were repelled by him.
translations.idiomatic: They assaulted the city again and again, and each time he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 已而賊轉熾。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebellion grew still fiercer.

sentences.zh: 驥聞，立馳入汀州，調援兵四集。

translations.literal: When Ji heard of it, he immediately galloped into Tingzhou and mustered relief troops from all sides.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji heard the news, he galloped at once to Tingzhou and gathered relief forces from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 驥單騎詣賊壘。

translations.literal: Ji went alone on horseback to the bandit encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Ji rode alone to the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 賊不意御史猝至，皆擐甲露刃。

translations.literal: The bandits did not expect a censor to arrive so suddenly; all donned armor and bared their blades.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had not expected a censor to appear so suddenly; they armored themselves and drew their blades.

sentences.zh: 驥從容立馬，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Ji calmly sat his horse and instructed them on fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sat his horse calmly and addressed them on the consequences of their choices.

sentences.zh: 賊見其至誠，感悟泣下，歸附者千七百余戶。

translations.literal: The bandits saw his utmost sincerity, were moved to tears, and more than seventeen hundred households submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his sincerity, the rebels were moved to tears, and more than seventeen hundred households submitted.

sentences.zh: 給以牛種，俾復故業。

translations.literal: He gave them oxen and seed and had them resume their former occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He supplied them with oxen and seed so they could return to their former livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 惟賊首李宗政負固不服，遂與泉深入破之。

translations.literal: Only the bandit chieftain Li Zongzheng stubbornly refused submission; Ji then joined Quan in pressing deep and breaking him.
translations.idiomatic: Only the rebel chieftain Li Zongzheng held out stubbornly, so Ji joined Quan in a deep strike that broke his resistance.

sentences.zh: 泉力戰，為賊所害。

translations.literal: Quan fought with all his strength and was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Quan fought fiercely and was killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 驥吊死恤傷，激以忠義，復與賊戰。

translations.literal: Ji mourned the dead and comforted the wounded, roused them with talk of loyalty and righteousness, and again fought the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ji mourned the dead, tended the wounded, and roused his men with appeals to loyalty and duty before fighting the rebels again.

sentences.zh: 連破十八寨，俘斬八百余人，四境悉平。

translations.literal: In succession he broke eighteen stockades, captured and beheaded more than eight hundred men, and the four quarters were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He captured eighteen stockades in succession, killed or captured more than eight hundred rebels, and pacified the entire region.

sentences.zh: 而驥冒瘴癘成疾，班師至上杭卒。

translations.literal: But Ji had braved miasma and pestilence and fell ill; as the army withdrew he died at Shanghang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had contracted a malarial fever in the pestilential lowlands, and he died at Shanghang as the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 軍民哀之如父母，旦夕臨者數千人，爭出財立祠。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians mourned him as they would parents; morning and evening several thousand came to pay respects, and they vied to contribute funds to build a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians mourned him as they would a parent. Thousands came day and night to pay their respects, and they competed to donate funds for a memorial shrine.

sentences.zh: 成化中以知縣蕭宏請，詔與泉並祀，賜祠名「褒忠」。

translations.literal: During Chenghua, at the request of the county magistrate Xiao Hong, an edict ordered joint sacrifice with Quan and granted the shrine the name "Praise Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign, at the petition of County Magistrate Xiao Hong, the court ordered Ji and Quan worshipped together and named the shrine "Praise Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 毛吉，字宗吉，余姚人。

translations.literal: Mao Ji, style Zongji, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Ji, styled Zongji, was from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the fifth year of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 除刑部廣東司主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Guangdong Bureau of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal clerk in the Guangdong Bureau of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 司轄錦衣衛。

translations.literal: The bureau had jurisdiction over the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That bureau had jurisdiction over the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 衛卒伺百官陰事，以片紙入奏即獲罪，公卿大夫莫不惴恐。

translations.literal: The guard soldiers watched officials' secret affairs; with a slip of paper submitted to the throne one immediately incurred guilt, and none among the grand ministers and great officers was not fearful and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Guard soldiers spied on officials' private affairs, and a single slip of paper sent to the throne could ruin a career. Grand ministers and high officials lived in constant dread.

sentences.zh: 公行請屬，狎侮官司，即以罪下刑部者，亦莫敢捶撻。

translations.literal: When out on official business they sought favors, treated government offices with disrespect and contempt, and even those sent to the Ministry of Justice on criminal charges—none dared beat them with rods.
translations.idiomatic: On their rounds they solicited favors and treated official offices with contempt, and even when guards were sent to the Ministry of Justice on criminal charges, no one dared beat them.

sentences.zh: 吉獨執法不撓，有犯必重懲之。

translations.literal: Ji alone enforced the law without yielding; if there was an offense he invariably punished it severely.
translations.idiomatic: Ji alone enforced the law without flinching and punished every offense to the full extent of the statutes.

sentences.zh: 其長門達怙寵肆虐，百官道遇率避馬，吉獨舉鞭拱手過，達怒甚。

translations.literal: Their chief Men Da relied on favor and rampaged at will; officials meeting him on the road for the most part avoided his horse, but Ji alone raised his whip, joined his hands, and passed by; Da was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Their commander Men Da abused his imperial favor and terrorized the capital. Officials who met him on the road usually dismounted and gave way, but Ji alone rode past with a salute of his whip. Men Da was furious.

sentences.zh: 吉以疾失朝，下錦衣獄。

translations.literal: Ji missed court on account of illness and was sent down to the Embroidered Uniform prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji missed court because of illness, he was thrown into the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 達大喜，簡健卒，用巨梃搒之。

translations.literal: Da was greatly pleased; he selected stalwart soldiers and beat him with huge cudgels.
translations.idiomatic: Men Da was delighted. He picked his strongest guards and had Ji beaten with heavy clubs.

sentences.zh: 肉潰見骨，不死。

translations.literal: His flesh putrefied until bone showed, yet he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: His flesh rotted away until the bone showed, yet he survived.

sentences.zh: 天順五年擢廣東僉事，分巡惠、潮二府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianshun he was promoted to Guangdong assistant surveillance commissioner, with separate jurisdiction over the two prefectures of Huizhou and Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianshun he was promoted to Guangdong assistant surveillance commissioner with jurisdiction over Huizhou and Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 痛仰豪右，民大悅。

translations.literal: He severely repressed powerful local families; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He cracked down hard on powerful local families, to the great delight of the common people.

sentences.zh: 及期當代，相率籲留之。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he was due to be replaced, they joined together in pleading that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and a successor was due, the people petitioned en masse to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 程鄉賊楊輝者，故劇賊羅劉寧黨也。

translations.literal: The bandit Yang Hui of Chengxiang was formerly a follower of the notorious bandit Luo Liuning.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel named Yang Hui of Chengxiang had once belonged to the notorious bandit Luo Liuning's faction.

sentences.zh: 已撫復叛，與其黨曾玉、謝瑩分據寶龍、石坑諸洞，攻陷江西安遠，剽閩、廣間。

translations.literal: Having once been pacified he rebelled again; with his followers Zeng Yu and Xie Ying he divided and held the caves of Baolong, Shikeng, and others, seized Jiangxi's Anyuan, and plundered between Fujian and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting once, he rebelled again. With his lieutenants Zeng Yu and Xie Ying he seized the cave strongholds of Baolong and Shikeng, overran Anyuan in Jiangxi, and raided across Fujian and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 已，欲攻程鄉。

translations.literal: Before long he intended to attack Chengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then set his sights on Chengxiang.

sentences.zh: 吉先其未至，募壯士合官軍得七百人。

translations.literal: Before they arrived Ji, ahead of them, recruited stalwart men and combined them with government troops to obtain seven hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Ji moved before they could arrive, recruiting stalwart fighters and joining them with government troops until he had seven hundred men.

sentences.zh: 抵賊巢。

translations.literal: He reached the bandit lair.
translations.idiomatic: He marched straight to the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 先破石坑，斬玉；

translations.literal: First he broke Shikeng and beheaded Yu;
translations.idiomatic: He first stormed Shikeng and killed Zeng Yu;

sentences.zh: 次擊瑩，馘之。

translations.literal: next he struck Ying and took his head.
translations.idiomatic: then he attacked Xie Ying and took his head.

sentences.zh: 復生擒輝。

translations.literal: He again captured Hui alive.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Yang Hui alive.

sentences.zh: 諸洞悉破，凡俘斬千四百人。

translations.literal: All the caves were thoroughly broken; in all more than fourteen hundred were captured or beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Every cave stronghold was overrun, and more than fourteen hundred rebels were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，憲宗進吉副使，璽書嘉勞。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported, the Chenghua Emperor promoted Ji to vice commissioner and sent an imperial seal letter commending and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory reached the court, the Chenghua Emperor promoted Ji to vice surveillance commissioner and sent an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 移巡高、雷、廉三府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to tour the three prefectures of Gaozhou, Leizhou, and Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to oversee Gaozhou, Leizhou, and Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時民遭賊躪，數百里無人煙，諸將悉閉城自守，或以賊告，反被撻。

translations.literal: At the time the people suffered bandit trampling; for several hundred li there was no human habitation; the various generals all closed the cities and held themselves in defense, and some who reported bandits were instead beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The people had been ravaged by bandits, and for hundreds of li the land lay deserted. Generals everywhere shut themselves inside their city walls, and some who reported rebel sightings were beaten for their trouble.

sentences.zh: 有自賊中逸歸者，輒誣以通賊，撲殺之。

translations.literal: Those who escaped and returned from among the bandits were promptly falsely accused of colluding with bandits and beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees who escaped from the rebels were often falsely accused of collusion and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 吉不勝憤，以平賊為己任。

translations.literal: Ji could not contain his anger and took pacifying the bandits as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was outraged and made pacifying the rebels his personal mission.

sentences.zh: 按部雷州。

translations.literal: He inspected the department at Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He toured Leizhou on inspection.

sentences.zh: 海康知縣王騏，雲南太和人也，日以義激其民，賊至輒奮擊。

translations.literal: The Haikang county magistrate Wang Qi, a native of Taihe in Yunnan, daily roused his people with righteousness; when bandits came he always fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate of Haikang, Wang Qi, a native of Taihe in Yunnan, daily roused his people with appeals to duty, and whenever bandits appeared he fought them fiercely.

sentences.zh: 吉壯其勇節，獎勵之。

translations.literal: Ji admired his courage and integrity and encouraged and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji admired his courage and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 適報賊掠鄉聚，吉與騏各率所部擊敗之。

translations.literal: Just then came report that bandits were plundering village settlements; Ji and Qi each led their detachments and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Word then came that rebels were raiding nearby villages, and Ji and Qi each led their forces out and routed them.

sentences.zh: 薦騏，遷雷州通判。

translations.literal: Ji recommended Qi, and he was transferred to be subprefect of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji recommended Qi for promotion, and he was appointed subprefect of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 未聞命，戰死。

translations.literal: Before the appointment was received, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment reached him, he was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈同知，蔭其子為國子生。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted vice prefect and his son was granted yin privilege as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously granted him the rank of vice prefect and enrolled his son in the Imperial Academy by yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 方吉出軍時，賫千金犒，委驛丞余文司出入，已用十之三。

translations.literal: When Ji was setting out with the army, he brought a thousand ounces of gold as reward bounty and entrusted the post station assistant Yu Wen to manage disbursement; three tenths had already been used.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji marched out with his troops, he brought a thousand ounces of silver in reward funds and entrusted Post Station Assistant Yu Wen with their disbursement. Nearly a third had already been spent.

sentences.zh: 吉既死，文憫其家貧，以所余金授吉仆，使持歸治喪。

translations.literal: After Ji had died, Wen pitied his family's poverty and gave the remaining gold to Ji's servant, having him carry it back to arrange the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji's death, Wen took pity on his family's poverty and gave the remaining funds to Ji's servant to carry home for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 是夜，仆婦忽坐中堂作吉語，顧左右曰：「請夏憲長來。」

translations.literal: That night the servant's wife suddenly sat in the central hall speaking in Ji's voice, turned to those beside her and said: "Please have Chief Censor Xia come."
translations.idiomatic: That night the maid suddenly seated herself in the main hall and spoke in Ji's voice, then turned to those around her and said, "Please ask Chief Censor Xia to come."

sentences.zh: 舉家大驚，走告按察使夏塤。

translations.literal: The whole household was greatly alarmed and ran to inform the surveillance commissioner Xia Kun.
translations.idiomatic: The entire household was terrified and rushed to tell Surveillance Commissioner Xia Kun.
