sentences.zh: 塤至。

translations.literal: Kun arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Kun came at once.

sentences.zh: 起揖曰：「吉受國恩，不幸死於賊。

translations.literal: She rose and bowed and said: "Ji received the state's grace and unhappily died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: She rose, bowed, and said, "Ji received the state's grace and met an untimely death at the hands of bandits.

sentences.zh: 今余文以所遺官銀付吉家，雖無文簿可考，吉負垢地下矣。

translations.literal: Now Yu Wen has given the remaining official silver to Ji's family; though there is no written account book by which to verify it, Ji would bear a stain in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yu Wen has given the remaining official silver to my family. Even though there is no ledger to account for it, I would bear this stain in the grave.

sentences.zh: 願亟還官，毋汙我。」

translations.literal: I wish it swiftly returned to the government; do not defile me."
translations.idiomatic: Please return it to the government at once and do not let this dishonor me."

sentences.zh: 言畢，仆地，頃之始蘇。

translations.literal: When the words were finished she fell to the ground; after a while she at last revived.
translations.idiomatic: When she had finished speaking, she collapsed. After a moment she came to her senses.

sentences.zh: 於是歸金於官。

translations.literal: Thereupon the gold was returned to the government.
translations.idiomatic: The silver was then returned to the government.

sentences.zh: 吉死時年四十，後賜謚忠襄。

translations.literal: When Ji died he was forty years old; later he was granted the posthumous title Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was forty when he died. He was later granted the posthumous title Zhongxiang, Loyal and Assisting.

sentences.zh: 林錦，字彥章，連江人。

translations.literal: Lin Jin, style Yanzhang, was a native of Lianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jin, styled Yanzhang, was from Lianjiang.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，由鄉貢授合浦訓導。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, through provincial recommendation he was appointed instructor at Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign, after graduating through provincial recommendation, he was appointed instructor at Hepu.

sentences.zh: 瑤寇充斥，內外無備。

translations.literal: Yao bandits filled the land; within and without there was no defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yao bandits swarmed the region, and the county was defenseless inside and out.

sentences.zh: 錦條具方略，悉中機宜。

translations.literal: Jin laid out plans in detail; all hit the strategic point.
translations.idiomatic: Jin submitted a detailed plan of action, and every measure proved sound.

sentences.zh: 巡撫葉盛異之，檄署靈山縣事。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Ye Sheng was impressed and by dispatch had him act as county affairs of Lingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ye Sheng was impressed and ordered him by dispatch to take charge of Lingshan County.

sentences.zh: 城毀於賊，錦因形便，為柵以守，廣設戰具，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: The city wall had been destroyed by bandits; Jin, following the terrain's advantage, built palisades for defense, widely set out war equipment, and the bandits did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The city walls had been destroyed by bandits. Jin used the terrain to build palisades, stocked them with weapons, and the rebels dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 滿秩去官，民曰：「公去，賊復至，誰禦者？」

translations.literal: When his term was complete he left office; the people said: "When the lord goes, the bandits will come again—who will defend?"
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he prepared to leave office, the people said, "When you go, the bandits will return. Who will defend us?"

sentences.zh: 悉逃入山。

translations.literal: All fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They all fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 盛以狀聞，詔即以錦為知縣。

translations.literal: Sheng reported the situation, and an edict immediately appointed Jin county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Sheng reported this to the court, and an edict immediately appointed Jin county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 馳驛之官，民復來歸。

translations.literal: He galloped by post relay to take office, and the people again came back.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled post-haste to take up his post, and the people returned.

sentences.zh: 適歲饑，諸瑤益剽掠無虛日。

translations.literal: Just then there was famine that year; the various Yao increased plundering with not a day free.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine struck, and Yao raids grew daily without respite.

sentences.zh: 錦單騎詣壘，曉以禍福。

translations.literal: Jin went alone on horseback to the encampment and instructed them on fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Jin rode alone to their camp and addressed them on the consequences of their choices.

sentences.zh: 瑤感悟，附縣二十五部鹹聽命。

translations.literal: The Yao were moved and submitted; twenty-five divisions attached to the county all alike obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao were moved to submit, and all twenty-five tribal divisions under the county came under his authority.

sentences.zh: 其不服者則討之。

translations.literal: Those who would not submit he then punished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who refused submission he attacked.

sentences.zh: 天順六年破賊羅禾水，再破之黃姜嶺，又大破之新莊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianshun he broke the bandits at Luoheshui, again broke them at Huangjiangling, and again broke them greatly at Xinzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianshun he defeated the rebels at Luoheshui, routed them again at Huangjiangling, and won a great victory at Xinzhuang.

sentences.zh: 先後斬獲千余級，還所掠人口，賊悉平，乃去柵，築土城。

translations.literal: In succession he beheaded and captured more than a thousand; he returned the people they had plundered; the bandits were all pacified; then he removed the palisades and built an earthen city wall.
translations.idiomatic: In these campaigns he killed or captured more than a thousand rebels, recovered the people they had seized, and pacified them entirely. He then dismantled the palisades and built an earthen city wall.

sentences.zh: 盛及監司屢薦其才。

translations.literal: Sheng and the surveillance officials repeatedly recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Sheng and the provincial overseers repeatedly recommended him for his ability.

sentences.zh: 成化改元，會廉州為賊所陷，乃以錦為試知府。

translations.literal: When the reign title changed to Chenghua, it happened that Lianzhou had been seized by bandits, and Jin was therefore appointed acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chenghua reign began, Lianzhou fell to bandits, and Jin was appointed acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 歲復大饑，賊四出劫掠。

translations.literal: That year famine returned on a great scale; bandits went out in all directions to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck again that year, and bandits ranged far and wide in pillaging raids.

sentences.zh: 錦諭散千余人，誅梗化者，而綏輯其流移。

translations.literal: Jin admonished and dispersed more than a thousand men, executed those stubborn against pacification, and settled and organized the displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Jin persuaded more than a thousand men to disband, put the recalcitrant to death, and brought order to the homeless wanderers.

sentences.zh: 境內悉平。

translations.literal: Within the borders all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The entire territory was pacified.

sentences.zh: 四年，上官交薦，請改授憲職，令專備欽、廉群盜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, superiors repeatedly recommended him, requesting transfer to a surveillance post, that he be charged exclusively with guarding against the bandit hordes of Qin and Lian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his superiors jointly recommended him for reassignment to the censorate, with sole responsibility for suppressing the outlaw gangs of Qinzhou and Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃以為按察使僉事，益勤於政。

translations.literal: He was then appointed assistant surveillance commissioner, and applied himself to governance with redoubled diligence.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an assistant regional inspector and threw himself even more zealously into his duties.

sentences.zh: 十年賜敕旌異。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an imperial edict was bestowed honoring his exceptional merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the throne issued an edict singling him out for special praise.

sentences.zh: 久之，進副使。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 錦以所部屢有盜警，思為經久計，乃設團河營於西，設新寮營於南，而別設洪崖營以杜諸寇出沒路。

translations.literal: Because Jin's jurisdiction repeatedly had bandit alarms, he sought a lasting plan: he established Tuanhe Camp in the west, Xinlao Camp in the south, and separately established Hongya Camp to block the routes by which raiders came and went.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit raids kept flaring across Jin's district, so he looked to a permanent solution: Tuanhe Camp in the west, Xinlao Camp in the south, and Hongya Camp on a separate line to seal off the raiders' routes of ingress and egress.

sentences.zh: 易靈山土城，更築高墉，亙五百丈，卒為巖邑。

translations.literal: He replaced Lingshan's earthen walls, built high ramparts in their stead extending five hundred zhang, and ultimately made it a fortified stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: He tore down Lingshan's mud fortifications and raised high walls five hundred zhang long, turning the county into a rock-hard bastion.

sentences.zh: 十四年，兵部上其撫輯功，被賚。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Ministry of War memorialized his pacification achievements, and he received imperial rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the war office reported his success in restoring order, and he was rewarded by the throne.

sentences.zh: 錦在兵間，以教化為務。

translations.literal: While Jin was among the armies, he made civil instruction his task.
translations.idiomatic: Even amid military campaigns, Jin made moral instruction his foremost concern.

sentences.zh: 靈山尚鬼，則禁淫祠，修學校，勸農桑。

translations.literal: Lingshan honored ghosts; he therefore banned illicit shrines, repaired schools, and urged farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshan was sunk in spirit worship; he outlawed improper shrines, restored the schools, and promoted agriculture and silk.

sentences.zh: 其治廉、欽，皆飭學宮，振起文教。

translations.literal: In governing Lian and Qin, in both he ordered the academies and revived literary culture.
translations.idiomatic: Whether governing Lianzhou or Qinzhou, he refurbished the Confucian halls and revived learning and culture.

sentences.zh: 為人誠實，洞見肺腑，瑤蠻莫不愛信。

translations.literal: As a man he was sincere and honest, with his innermost heart fully visible; Yao tribesmen and barbarians none failed to love and trust him.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly sincere—his heart lay open to all—and Yao and tribal peoples alike loved and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 其行軍，與士卒同甘苦，有功輒推以與人，以故士多效死，所在祠祀。

translations.literal: When he marched, he shared hardship and comfort with the soldiers; whenever there was merit he forthwith ceded it to others—hence the troops often gave their lives in his service, and wherever he had been they enshrined and worshipped him.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he ate and suffered as his men did; credit for every success he gave away. For that soldiers gladly died for him, and shrines rose to him wherever he had served.

sentences.zh: 郭緒，字繼業，太康人。

translations.literal: Guo Xu, courtesy name Jiye, was a native of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xu, style name Jiye, came from Taikang.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of Chenghua 17.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 使楚府，卻其饋。

translations.literal: Sent on a mission to the Prince of Chu's domain, he declined gifts offered him.
translations.idiomatic: On mission to the Princedom of Chu, he refused its presents.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，督餉二十萬於陜西給軍。

translations.literal: Appointed a chief clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, he supervised two hundred thousand [units of] provisions in Shaanxi to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Made a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, he oversaw two hundred thousand units of grain pay in Shaanxi for the troops.

sentences.zh: 主者以羨告，悉還之。

translations.literal: The custodian reported a surplus; he returned it all.
translations.idiomatic: When the manager reported a surplus, he sent every bit of it back.

sentences.zh: 歷遷雲南參議。

translations.literal: He successively rose to Yunnan assistant administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to assistant commissioner in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 初，孟密宣撫司之設也，實割木邦宣慰司地。

translations.literal: At first, when the Mengmi Pacification Commission was established, it in fact carved off territory from the Meng Ban Regional Command.
translations.idiomatic: The Mengmi Pacification Commission had originally been carved out of the Mu-Bang Regional Command.

sentences.zh: 既而孟密思揲復於界外侵木邦地二十七所。

translations.literal: Afterwards Mengmi's Si Die again beyond the border encroached on twenty-seven places of Meng Ban territory.
translations.idiomatic: Later Si Die of Mengmi seized twenty-seven Mu-Bang holdings beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 屬諭之還。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly admonished him to return them.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly ordered him to give them back.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 乃調孟養宣撫思祿兵脅之。

translations.literal: The court therefore mobilized the troops of Mengyang Pacification Commissioner Si Lu to coerce him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then mobilized Si Lu of Mengyang to pressure him by force.

sentences.zh: 思揲始還所侵地，然多殺孟養兵。

translations.literal: Si Die at last returned the encroached territory, yet killed many Mengyang soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Si Die finally restored the seized land—but slaughtered many of Mengyang's troops in the process.

sentences.zh: 思祿仇之，發兵越金沙江奪木邦故割孟密地十有三所。

translations.literal: Si Lu held a grudge, raised troops, crossed the Jinsha River, and seized thirteen places of the old Meng Ban territory that had been carved off to Mengmi.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lu nursed a grievance, crossed the Jinsha with an army, and retook thirteen of the old Mu-Bang districts ceded to Mengmi.

sentences.zh: 兩酋構怨不已。

translations.literal: The two chieftains nursed enmity without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The two chiefs remained locked in feud.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳金承詔，遣緒與副使曹玉往諭之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Chen Jin, obeying the imperial edict, dispatched Xu and Vice Commissioner Cao Yu to go admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on imperial orders, Grand Coordinator Chen Jin sent Xu and Deputy Commissioner Cao Yu to reason with them.

sentences.zh: 旬余抵金齒。

translations.literal: After ten-odd days they reached Jinchi.
translations.idiomatic: In little over ten days they reached Jinchi.

sentences.zh: 參將盧和先統軍距所據地二程而舍，遣官馳驛往諭，皆留不報。

translations.literal: The assistant regional commander Lu He had first led troops to encamp two stages from their held territory, sent officials by courier to admonish them, but all were detained without reply.
translations.idiomatic: Lu He, the deputy commander, had camped his force two stages short of the chiefs' holdings and sent envoys by relay post; every envoy was held and never answered.

sentences.zh: 和懼，還軍至幹崖遇緒，語故，戒勿進。

translations.literal: He, in fear, withdrew his army; at Ganya he met Xu, told him the reason, and warned him not to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Lu He fell back; at Ganya he met Xu, explained what had happened, and urged him not to go forward.

sentences.zh: 緒不可。

translations.literal: Xu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xu refused.

sentences.zh: 玉以疾辭。

translations.literal: Yu pleaded illness and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yu begged off, claiming illness.

sentences.zh: 緒遂單騎從數人行，旬日至南甸，峻險不可騎，乃斬棘徒步引繩以登。

translations.literal: Xu then alone on horseback with several men traveling, in ten days reached Nandian; the steep perilous [terrain] would not allow riding, so he cut through brambles, went on foot, and pulled himself up by ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu rode on alone with a handful of companions. Ten days later they reached Nandian, where the cliffs were too sheer for horses; he hacked through thorns and climbed on foot, hauling himself up by ropes.

sentences.zh: 又旬日至一大澤。

translations.literal: Another ten days and they reached a great marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days more brought them to a vast swamp.

sentences.zh: 土官以象輿來，緒乘之往。

translations.literal: A native official brought an elephant carriage; Xu mounted it and went on.
translations.idiomatic: A local chieftain sent an elephant howdah; Xu rode it onward.

sentences.zh: 行毒霧中，泥沙踸踔。

translations.literal: Traveling in poisonous mists, [they] sank deep in mud and sand.
translations.idiomatic: They passed through poison mists, sinking deep in mire and sand at every step.

sentences.zh: 又旬日至孟賴，去金沙江僅二舍。

translations.literal: Another ten days and they reached Menglai, only two stages from the Jinsha River.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later they arrived at Menglai, a bare two marches from the Jinsha.

sentences.zh: 手自為檄，使持過江，諭以朝廷招徠意。

translations.literal: He himself wrote a proclamation, had it carried across the river, and admonished them regarding the court's intent to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a proclamation himself, sent it across the river, and set forth the court's wish to bring them back into the fold.

sentences.zh: 蠻人相顧驚曰：「中國使竟至此乎？」

translations.literal: The barbarians looked at one another in alarm and said: "A Chinese envoy has actually come this far?"
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen stared at one another in shock: "An envoy of China has truly come this far?"

sentences.zh: 發兵率象馬數萬夜渡江，持長槊勁弩，環之數重。

translations.literal: They raised troops leading tens of thousands of elephants and horses, crossed the river by night, bearing long spears and powerful crossbows, and surrounded them in several rings.
translations.idiomatic: They mustered tens of thousands of elephants and horses, crossed the river by night armed with long spears and heavy crossbows, and ringed him round in layer after layer.

sentences.zh: 從行者懼，請勿進。

translations.literal: Those accompanying him were afraid and asked that he not advance.
translations.idiomatic: His escort panicked and begged him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 緒拔刀叱曰：「明日必渡江，敢阻者斬！」

translations.literal: Xu drew his sword and shouted: "Tomorrow I shall certainly cross the river—whoever dares block me shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu bared his blade and roared: "I cross the river tomorrow. Stand in my way and you die!"

sentences.zh: 思祿既得檄，見譬曉禍福甚備，又聞至者才數人，乃遣酋長來聽令，且致饋。

translations.literal: When Si Lu had received the proclamation and seen how thoroughly the blessings and calamities were explained, and also heard that those who had come numbered only a few men, he then dispatched chieftains to hear orders and moreover sent gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Once Si Lu read the proclamation—with its exhaustive lesson on reward and ruin—and learned that only a handful of men had come, he sent chieftains to take orders and offered presents.

sentences.zh: 緒卻之，出敕諭宣示。

translations.literal: Xu refused them, produced the imperial edict of admonition, and proclaimed it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu declined the gifts, produced the throne's directive, and read it aloud.

sentences.zh: 思祿亦繼至。

translations.literal: Si Lu also came in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lu arrived shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 緒先敘其勞，次白其冤狀，然後責其叛。

translations.literal: Xu first recounted their labors, next stated their grievances, and then rebuked them for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Xu first acknowledged their services, then voiced their complaints, and only then censured them for defiance.

sentences.zh: 諸酋聞，鹹俯伏呼萬歲，請歸侵地。

translations.literal: When the chieftains heard, all prostrated themselves and cried "Long live [the emperor]!", requesting to return the encroached territory.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs prostrated themselves and shouted their allegiance, pledging to restore all seized lands.

sentences.zh: 緒詰前所留使人，乃盡出而歸之。

translations.literal: Xu demanded the envoys previously detained; they were all released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xu demanded the envoys Lu He had left behind; they were freed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 和及玉聞報馳至，則已歸地納款矣。

translations.literal: He and Yu, hearing the report, galloped there, but [Xu] had already restored the land and submitted allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Lu He and Cao Yu raced up when word arrived—only to find the land already restored and peace secured.

sentences.zh: 時弘治十四年五月也。

translations.literal: It was the fifth month of Hongzhi 14.
translations.idiomatic: This was May of the fourteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 越三年，擢緒四川督儲參政。

translations.literal: Three years later Xu was promoted to Sichuan grain-supply administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on he was promoted to grain-supply commissioner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，始以雲南功，加俸一級。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong emperor acceded, only then for his Yunnan achievements was one rank of salary added.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wuzong emperor took the throne, his Yunnan service was finally recognized with a one-step rise in stipend.

sentences.zh: 明年致仕歸。

translations.literal: The next year he retired and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired and went home.

sentences.zh: 姜昂，字恒頫，太倉人。

translations.literal: Jiang Ang, courtesy name Hengfu, was a native of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ang, style name Hengfu, came from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 成化八年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of Chenghua 8.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the eighth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除棗強知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Zaoqiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Zaoqiang.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was granted the post of censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 偕同官劾方士李孜省，杖午門外。

translations.literal: Together with colleagues he impeached the Taoist adept Li Zisheng and was caned outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He joined fellow censors in indicting the sorcerer Li Zisheng and was flogged outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞改南，尋出為河南知府。

translations.literal: Because his mother was aged he requested transfer to the south; soon he was sent out as Henan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's age moved him to seek a southern post; he was soon sent out as prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 吏白事畢，退闔門讀書，鞭箠懸不用。

translations.literal: When clerks had reported business finished, he retired, closed his doors to read books; the whip and flogging staff hung unused.
translations.idiomatic: When the day's petitions were done he shut his door to read; the whip and bastinado hung idle on the wall.

sentences.zh: 藩府人有犯，立決遣之。

translations.literal: When persons of the princely household committed offenses, he immediately judged and dispatched them.
translations.idiomatic: Princely retainers who broke the law he tried and punished on the spot.

sentences.zh: 改知寧波，擢福建參政。

translations.literal: Transferred to be prefect of Ningbo, promoted to Fujian assistant administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Ningbo, then was promoted to assistant commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 請終養歸，服闋而卒。

translations.literal: He requested leave to go home for full filial mourning and returned; when the mourning period ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return home to nurse his mother through her final years; he died soon after the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 昂在官，日市少肉供母，而自食菜茹。

translations.literal: While Ang held office, daily he bought a little meat to supply his mother, while he himself ate vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: In office he bought a little meat each day for his mother and lived on greens himself.

sentences.zh: 子弟學書，不聽用官紙筆，家居室不蔽風雨。

translations.literal: For the younger generation studying books, he would not allow use of official paper and brushes; at home his dwelling did not shelter against wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: His children learned to write without official stationery; at home he lived in a roof that barely kept out the weather.

sentences.zh: 子龍，字夢賓，正德三年進士。

translations.literal: His son Long, courtesy name Mengbin, was a metropolitan graduate of Zhengde 3.
translations.idiomatic: His son Long, style name Mengbin, passed the palace examination in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as a director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 武宗南巡，率同官諫。

translations.literal: When Wuzong toured south, he led colleagues in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor set out on his southern tour, Long led fellow officials in memorializing against it.

sentences.zh: 罰跪五日，杖幾死。

translations.literal: Punished to kneel five days, caned nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: He was forced to kneel for five days and beaten within an inch of his life.

sentences.zh: 出為建寧同知，尋遷雲南副使，備兵瀾滄、姚安。

translations.literal: Sent out as Tongzhi of Jianning, soon transferred to Yunnan vice commissioner, garrisoning troops at Lancang and Yao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled to Jianning as deputy prefect, he was soon made Yunnan vice commissioner and charged with military affairs at Lancang and Yao'an.

sentences.zh: 滇故盜藪，龍讓土酋曰：「爾世官，縱盜寧非賄乎？」

translations.literal: Yunnan was formerly a thieves' den; Long reproached the native chieftain: "You hold hereditary office—allowing bandits, is this not bribery?"
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan had long been a robbers' nest; Long challenged the native chief: "Your post is hereditary—is letting bandits run free not simply taking bribes?"

sentences.zh: 酋懼，撫諭群盜，悉聽命。

translations.literal: The chieftain feared, soothed and admonished the bandit hordes, and all obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the chief pacified the outlaw bands, and they all submitted.

sentences.zh: 巨盜方定者，既降而貧，為妻妾所詬，卒不忍負龍，竟仰藥死。

translations.literal: The great bandit called Fang Ding, having surrendered and being poor, was reviled by his wife and concubines; in the end unable to betray Long, he ultimately drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Ding, a major outlaw, surrendered but lived in poverty; mocked by his wives and concubines, he could not bring himself to fail Long and finally took poison.

sentences.zh: 南安大盜千人，御史欲征兵，龍檄三日散盡。

translations.literal: At Nan'an a thousand great bandits; the censor wished to mobilize troops—Long's proclamation dispersed them within three days.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand bandits plagued Nan'an; when the censor wanted to call out the army, Long's edict dispersed them in three days.

sentences.zh: 四川鹽井剌馬仁、雲南曬江和歌仲讎殺數十年，龍撫諭，遂解。

translations.literal: Sichuan Salt Well's Lama Ren and Yunnan Shaijiang's Hege Zhong had feuded and killed for several decades; Long soothed and admonished them, and the feud was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Lama Ren of the Sichuan salt wells and Hege Zhong of Shaijiang in Yunnan had been blood-feuding for decades; Long's mediation ended it.

sentences.zh: 大候州土官猛國恃險肆暴，龍擒之。

translations.literal: Dahan Prefecture's native official Meng Guo relied on perilous terrain and committed rampant violence; Long captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guo, the tribal officer of Dahan, tyrannized from his mountain fastness until Long seized him.

sentences.zh: 在滇四年，番、漢大治。

translations.literal: Four years in Yunnan; tribal peoples and Han were greatly governed.
translations.idiomatic: In four years among them, both tribesmen and Han were brought to good order.

sentences.zh: 鄧川州立三正人祠，祀袁州郭紳、莆田林俊及龍。

translations.literal: Dengchuan Prefecture established a Shrine of Three Upright Men, enshrining Yuanzhou's Guo Shen, Putian's Lin Jun, and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Dengchuan erected a Hall of Three Worthies honoring Guo Shen of Yuanzhou, Lin Jun of Putian, and Long.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：陶成、陳敏諸人，以監司守令著征剿功，而成及毛吉、葉禎身死王事，勞烈顯著，亦可以愧戎帥之畏懦戚蹜者矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tao Cheng, Chen Min, and others won fame as surveillance officials and magistrates for pacification achievements; Cheng and Mao Ji and Ye Zhen died in imperial service—their meritorious fervor conspicuous—this may also put to shame military commanders who are timid, cringing, and shrink back.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: Tao Cheng, Chen Min, and their fellows won renown as provincial overseers and magistrates for suppressing rebellion; Cheng, Mao Ji, and Ye Zhen died in the emperor's service—their heroic sacrifice stands bright—and they might well shame the cowardly, cringing commanders who hang back from the field.

sentences.zh: 林錦威能臨制，材足綏懷，邊疆皆得斯人，何憂不治？

translations.literal: Lin Jin's might could face and control; his talent sufficed to soothe and cherish—if the frontier everywhere obtained such a man, what worry would there be of no good governance?
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jin had the force to impose order and the gifts to win people over—if every border post had such a man, what frontier could fail to know peace?

sentences.zh: 郭緒單騎入險，諭服兩酋，令當洪、永間亦何至尚淹常調哉。

translations.literal: Guo Xu alone on horseback entered peril, admonished and pacified two chieftains—given men like this at Hongwu and Yongle, how could they still have been left stalled in routine postings?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xu rode alone into the wilds and talked two chiefs into submission—men like him in the days of Hongwu and Yongle would never have been left mouldering in ordinary ranks.

sentences.zh: 平世秉國者，多抑邊功，謂恐生事。

translations.literal: In peaceful times those holding the state often suppressed frontier achievements, saying they feared provoking incidents.
translations.idiomatic: In tranquil times those who ran the empire often downplayed border successes, lest they stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 然大帥倚內援，敘祿又多逾等，適足以長武夫玩寇之心，而無以獎勞臣致死之節。

translations.literal: Yet great commanders relied on inner-court backing; ranked salaries moreover often exceeded grades—this was just enough to lengthen military men's hearts of treating bandits lightly, and insufficient to reward and encourage ministers' integrity in giving their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yet frontier generals thrived on court patronage and drew pay above their rank—encouraging soldiers to treat the enemy lightly while doing nothing to honor those who died in the emperor's service.

sentences.zh: 國家以賞罰馭世，曷可不公乎！

translations.literal: The state governs the age by rewards and punishments—how can they not be fair!
translations.idiomatic: The realm rules through reward and punishment—how can they be anything but just!
